steps.title: Import Vue and composition API functions (ref, onMounted, onUnmounted)
steps.instruction: Import Vue, ref, onMounted, and onUnmounted from 'vue'
steps.hint: Use a single import statement to bring in all the necessary functions from the Vue package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing multiple functions from a module
import { useState, useEffect } from 'react'
steps.seedCode: // Import Vue, ref, onMounted, and onUnmounted from 'vue'
steps.expectedOutcome: The Vue composition API functions are imported and ready to use in your component.
successCriteria: Vue, ref, onMounted, and onUnmounted are imported from 'vue'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the Vue composition API functions needed for reactive state and lifecycle hooks.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close, but make sure you're importing all four items: Vue, ref, onMounted, and onUnmounted from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to import Vue, ref, onMounted, and onUnmounted from the 'vue' package.

steps.title: Create the main App component
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named App using defineComponent or a setup function. The component should return a template with a root <div> element.
steps.hint: In Vue, you can define a component using defineComponent or a setup function. The component must return a template.
steps.seedCode:
// Import Vue, ref, onMounted, and onUnmounted from 'vue'

// Create the App component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional Vue component named App is created with a root <div> in its template.
successCriteria: The App component is defined using defineComponent or a setup function and returns a template with a root <div>.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the main App component. This sets up the foundation for building the session timeout hook.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started creating the component, but make sure it's named App and returns a template with a root <div> element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component isn't properly defined. Ensure you use defineComponent or a setup function and return a template with a root <div>.

steps.title: Initialize session timeout state with ref
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, initialize a reactive state variable called 'isSessionExpired' using ref, with a default value of false.
steps.hint: Use the ref function you imported earlier to create reactive state. The syntax is: const isSessionExpired = ref(false)
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating reactive state for a toggle
const isVisible = ref(false);
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a reactive state variable 'isSessionExpired' initialized to false inside the setup function.
successCriteria: The App component's setup function contains 'const isSessionExpired = ref(false)'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created reactive state to track session timeout status.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using ref() with the correct default value (false) and assigning it to a variable named 'isSessionExpired'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The session timeout state wasn't initialized correctly. Remember to use ref() inside the setup function.

steps.title: Initialize timer reference with ref
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, create a reactive reference called 'timeoutId' using ref, initialized with null.
steps.hint: Use the ref function imported earlier to create a reactive reference. The syntax is: const timeoutId = ref(null);
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating a reactive reference for a timer ID
const timerRef = ref(null);
steps.expectedOutcome: A reactive reference 'timeoutId' is created with an initial value of null, ready to store the timeout ID for session management.
successCriteria: The 'timeoutId' reference is created using ref and initialized with null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a reactive reference for the timeout ID. This will allow us to track and clear the timeout when needed.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the ref function to create the reference and initializing it with null.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to create a reactive reference called 'timeoutId' using the ref function and set its initial value to null.

steps.title: Define resetSessionTimeout function
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, define a function named resetSessionTimeout that clears any existing timeout and sets a new 10-second timeout.
steps.hint: Use clearTimeout to clear the timer reference value, then set a new setTimeout that updates the session timeout state to true after 10000 milliseconds.
steps.expectedOutcome: The resetSessionTimeout function will be defined, ready to clear and restart the session timeout timer.
successCriteria: A function named resetSessionTimeout is defined that clears the existing timeout and sets a new 10-second timeout.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the resetSessionTimeout function that will manage the session timeout timer.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it clears the existing timeout and sets a new 10-second timeout that updates sessionTimeout to true.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't defined correctly. It should clear any existing timeout and set a new 10-second timeout that sets sessionTimeout to true.

steps.title: Define handleUserActivity function
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, define a function named handleUserActivity that calls the resetSessionTimeout function when invoked.
steps.hint: Create a simple function that calls your existing resetSessionTimeout function. This will be triggered by user activity events later.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a handleUserActivity function that calls resetSessionTimeout, preparing to respond to user interactions.
successCriteria: A function named handleUserActivity is defined and calls resetSessionTimeout.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the handleUserActivity function that will reset the session timeout when users interact with the page.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've defined a function named handleUserActivity that calls resetSessionTimeout.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleUserActivity function isn't defined correctly. Create a function with that name that calls resetSessionTimeout.

steps.title: Set up event listeners in onMounted
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, use Vue's onMounted lifecycle hook to add event listeners for 'mousemove' and 'keydown' events that will call your handleUserActivity function.
steps.hint: Call onMounted with a callback function. Inside that callback, use window.addEventListener for both event types.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will now automatically start listening for user activity when it mounts to the DOM.
successCriteria: onMounted is called with a callback that adds both 'mousemove' and 'keydown' event listeners to the window object, each calling handleUserActivity.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully set up the event listeners that will detect user activity and reset the session timeout.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added the onMounted hook, but make sure you're adding both event listeners ('mousemove' and 'keydown') and calling handleUserActivity.
steps.feedbackWrong: The event listeners aren't set up correctly. Remember to use onMounted to add both 'mousemove' and 'keydown' listeners that call handleUserActivity.

steps.title: Clean up event listeners in onUnmounted
steps.instruction: Add an onUnmounted hook inside the setup function to remove the 'mousemove' and 'keydown' event listeners and clear any active timeout.
steps.hint: Use onUnmounted from Vue to run cleanup code when the component is destroyed. Inside it, call removeEventListener for both events and clearTimeout with timerRef.value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will properly clean up event listeners and timeouts when it unmounts, preventing memory leaks.
successCriteria: An onUnmounted hook is added that removes both 'mousemove' and 'keydown' event listeners and clears the timeout using timerRef.value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added cleanup logic to prevent memory leaks when the component unmounts.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added onUnmounted, but make sure to remove both event listeners ('mousemove' and 'keydown') and clear the timeout.
steps.feedbackWrong: The cleanup step is missing or incomplete. Add an onUnmounted hook that removes event listeners and clears the timeout.

steps.title: Return template structure with conditional rendering
steps.instruction: Inside the App component's setup function, return a template object that conditionally renders different content based on the sessionTimeout value. When sessionTimeout is true, show a session expired message. When false, show a normal session active message.
steps.hint: The return statement should include a template object with conditional rendering using v-if or a ternary expression. You can use sessionTimeout.value to check the state.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component now returns a template that conditionally displays content based on the sessionTimeout state, showing either a session expired or active message.
successCriteria: The setup function returns a template object with conditional rendering that checks sessionTimeout.value and displays appropriate messages.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added conditional rendering to show different messages based on the session state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your template properly checks sessionTimeout.value and shows both the expired and active messages.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't yet conditionally render based on sessionTimeout. Review how to use v-if or ternary expressions in Vue templates.

steps.title: Add refresh button and wire click event
steps.instruction: In the template's return statement, add a button element with the text 'Refresh Session' that calls the resetSessionTimeout function when clicked.
steps.hint: Use the @click directive to attach the resetSessionTimeout function to the button's click event.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button with click handler
<button @click="handleClick">Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button labeled 'Refresh Session' appears in the UI, and clicking it resets the session timeout.
successCriteria: The template includes a button element with @click="resetSessionTimeout" and displays 'Refresh Session' text.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the refresh button and wired it to reset the session timeout.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it calls resetSessionTimeout on click and has the correct text.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or not properly connected to resetSessionTimeout. Check the @click directive and button text.
